evidence: product-price.validator.ts: ProductPriceValidator.addRules rejects `this.subject.props.price.getValue() <= 0` ('Price must be greater than 0') and `> 1000000`.

product-status.validator.ts: ProductStatusValidator.addRules rejects `status === ProductStatus.ACTIVE && this.subject.props.price.getValue() === 0` ('Cannot activate product with zero price'). Any zero price already breaks the rule in ProductPriceValidator, so this check is a duplicate.
product-business-rules.validator.ts: ProductBusinessRulesValidator.addRules adds a second price ceiling, `price > nameLength * 10000`. Its comment says '1000 veces', which does not match the code.
product-business-rules.validator.ts: the description-vs-name length rule sits apart from ProductDescriptionValidator in product-description.validator.ts, which only checks presence.
All five classes extend AbstractRuleValidator<Product> and use addBrokenRule('props.<field>', ...), so they share one abstraction.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All five files serve one concern: validating the Product aggregate. They all extend AbstractRuleValidator<Product> and report failures through addBrokenRule, so the abstraction is used consistently. However, the price invariant is not kept in one place. ProductPriceValidator already enforces price > 0 (it rejects price <= 0). ProductStatusValidator encodes a second, weaker copy of that rule (an active product cannot have price === 0). Price upper bounds are also split: ProductPriceValidator has a fixed maximum of 1000000, and ProductBusinessRulesValidator adds a maximum tied to name length, with a comment that says 1000 while the code uses 10000. Description rules are likewise split between ProductDescriptionValidator (required) and ProductBusinessRulesValidator (at least as long as the name). This scattering and duplication of invariants matches the rubric's fail condition.

violations.message: ProductStatusValidator re-implements a price invariant (an active product cannot have price === 0) that ProductPriceValidator already enforces with price <= 0. The price lower bound is duplicated outside the price validator.

ProductBusinessRulesValidator defines a second price ceiling (price > nameLength * 10000; the comment says 1000) and a description rule, splitting price and description invariants away from ProductPriceValidator and ProductDescriptionValidator.
